ideas.description: Follow up E045 on the head lr axis. On the tip (E047 commit 3d6a396: bs 1536, 20 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5 then 32 px, 6.75 epochs, SGD-group lr x1.5, head lr x2 with wd halved, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8 NS3, lookahead 0.97^5, jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only; or I061's successor if it is kept), make one change: raise the head (final linear layer) lr multiplier from x2 to x3 relative to the original head lr. Keep lr*wd constant for the head by dividing its current wd by 1.5. BN-bias lr x64, whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, curriculum, jitter, bs and epochs stay identical. The lr is a 0-d tensor, so there are no new shapes and nothing recompiles. Background: head x0.5 cost 0.41 pp (E039) and x2 gained 0.18 pp (E045), so the head looks under-driven. This run checks whether the optimum lies above x2 before the head axis is closed.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.35 to +0.4 pp, point +0.05 pp (range 0.7515-0.759 around tip 0.7550); returns probably diminish past x2. Time unchanged within +-1.5% (~5.27 s). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.7.3: keep it, then pair the banked margin with a time cut (I061's 28 px stage, the 16 px first stage, or bs 2048). A result within +-0.2 pp puts the optimum near x2 and closes the head axis. A drop of 0.25 pp or more means x2 is the peak; revert.

ideas.description: Make the warmup-phase stage cheaper again, the next step after E047 (24 -> 20 px saved 3.5% at -0.18 pp). On the tip (E047, or I061's successor if it is kept, in which case change only its first stage), make one change: the first stage's resolution drops from 20 px to 16 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip/translate/jitter). The stage boundary (1.5 epochs, in samples), total epochs, bs 1536 and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged, so the sample stream and lr values are identical. In drafts/, first print the per-block spatial sizes at 16 px input. Expected: whitening 15, block1 15 -> pool 7, block2 7 -> pool 3, block3 3 -> pool 1, final map 1x1. The 16 px graph's final pool can then be a reshape/flatten of the 1x1 map, or F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to the final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (E009 Inductor bug). In build(), warm up the 16 px train step with and without whitening-bias grad at bs 1536, plus every partial-batch shape at the 1.5-epoch switch, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Check that total build time stays under ~450 s. Run debug_nan.py on the new graphs under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times. Eval stays the 32 px graph.
ideas.expected: Time -1% to -4%, point -2.7% (~5.13 s vs 5.273 s). Block-1 FLOPs per low-res step fall from ~0.38x to ~0.23x of a 32 px step, on ~22% of steps; per-step Muon/lookahead cost is unchanged. Accuracy -0.6 to +0.2 pp, point -0.2 pp (~0.7530, borderline); C0190 suggests a minimum useful size, and 16 px CIFAR loses a lot of detail. Feasible means a new best. If it misses 0.753 by 0.15 pp or less, keep the code path and pair it with the next accuracy gain (head x3, I054, I064). A drop of 0.4 pp or more means the warmup phase needs ~20 px of detail; then fix the first stage at 20 px and close lower resolutions.

ideas.description: Measure the paired re-draw noise on the current base directly, without changing any math. On the tip (E047, or I061's successor if it is kept), make one change: in prepare(), right after seeding the trial generator and before the epoch permutations and augmentation draws, consume one dummy draw from that same trial-seeded generator (e.g. torch.randn(1, generator=g, device=g.device)). Every permutation, flip, translate and jitter value then shifts while the recipe stays identical. Nothing else changes, so no new compiled shapes are needed. Report per-seed accuracies next to the tip's. Discard the run regardless of outcome: keeping a lucky RNG shift would select on seeds 0-2 and would not transfer to the 40-seed judge.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged within +-1.5%. Mean accuracy within +-0.2 pp of 0.7550, point 0; per-seed changes of about +-0.1-0.3 pp. A mean shift of 0.08 pp or less with per-seed |delta| of 0.15 pp or less supports H4.1.4: the paired sd on the Muon base is small, so keeps of ~+0.15-0.2 pp (E042, E045) are probably real and stack. A mean shift of 0.2 pp or more means pure re-draw is as large as the recent keeps and the 0.2 pp margin. In that case, later stacking predictions must carry +-0.25 pp, and time cuts need >=0.3 pp of banked margin before they are tried.

drop.reason: Its base no longer exists. It was written to trim 0.25 epoch from E045 (margin 0.38 pp), but the tip is now E047 with a 0.20 pp margin. At ~1.14 pp/epoch a 0.25-epoch trim costs ~0.29 pp, so it is infeasible by construction. Its trigger (I061 infeasible, applied to E045) also points at a superseded commit. Re-propose an epoch trim only after an accuracy gain of >=0.3 pp is banked.

Its expected outcome is a slower run (+0.9%), so it cannot be kept and does not move the score. Its only value is as a build-time fallback, and no build has come near the 600 s limit yet (E044: 232 s). Re-propose it only if a stacked curriculum/bs variant pushes build past ~450 s.

structured_output.summary: Tip is E047 (5.273 s, 0.7550, margin 0.20 pp). I061 (28 px stage) is running; its expected -0.23 pp would use up the whole margin. So the binding need is accuracy gains of ~0.2 pp that can be paired with the cheap time levers left: curriculum, bs 2048, a lower first-stage resolution. Each of those costs ~0.05 pp per 1% of time. Three ideas added: (1) head lr x3 (H1.7.3) as an exploit for margin, since the head axis is the only SGD-group lever that has responded so far. (2) A 16 px first stage (H2.3), extending the E047 trend for a ~2.7% time cut and pairing with any banked gain. (3) An RNG-shift diagnostic run (H4.1.4) that measures the paired re-draw sd on the current base directly; it is discarded whatever the result, to avoid selecting on seeds 0-2. That sd decides whether the +0.15-0.2 pp keeps can be stacked. Dropped I062: its trim is infeasible at the new 0.20 pp margin and it points at a superseded base. Dropped I065: expected slower, and build time is not binding yet. Queue is now 8: I054, I057, I058, I063, I064 plus the three new ideas. One note on D015: it read E046 (Muon lr 0.20) as recovering E041's loss, but E046 sat on the E045 base and was -0.10 pp against it. Keeping Muon lr 0.16 in I057 is therefore right.
